_comment: Frozen contract (SEC-25, SEC-27; tests/security/test_credential_isolation.py; SECSUITE frozen suite). Premise 4 in executable form: a subscription agent CLI is a third-party binary running with the user's local auth, so app/cloud secrets must not reach its process environment (SEC-25), and a secret must not resurface through the diagnostic path when that subprocess fails (SEC-27). Both probes are `sec_managed` -- they need harness-planted environment variables, so they AUTO-SKIP in attached mode and a language port that only runs attached mode never exercises them. Plan decision 44 extracts their inputs and expected refusals here so `SEC_BOOT_*_CMD` boot mode (planned, ~wk8) becomes a runner over data and any weakening is a reviewable diff. The ALLOWLIST itself is NOT duplicated here: it lives in fixtures/agent_env_allowlist.json, which SEC-25 checks the observed env against and SEC-42 pins the Python constant to. Changing this file is a security decision: it requires a docs/MODULE_INDEX.md ledger row and a SECSUITE_VERSION bump (see tests/security/README.md).

SEC-25._note: The observed subprocess env must be a SUBSET of the frozen allowlist, and no planted sentinel value may appear anywhere in it. Two independent checks: the key-set check catches a widened allowlist, the value check catches a secret smuggled under an allowlisted NAME (e.g. an API key pasted into PATH or HOME).

additional_sentinels._note: The four configured service bearer tokens are themselves secret material, so their live values join the sentinel set at run time.

SEC-27._note: A planted provider secret must not surface in the HTTP response body or in service diagnostics when the agent subprocess fails. The stub is told to exit non-zero AND write the secret to stderr, which is the realistic leak path: a provider error handler that echoes captured stderr verbatim.
